free_tier.stated: Each year the Innovative and Novel Computational Impact on Theory and Experiment (INCITE) program awards to researchers billions of supercomputer processor hours and 100 trillion bytes of data storage space
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The INCITE FAQ publishes no single-file cap; the award is an allocation of processor hours and data storage on POSIX and nearline file systems. At OLCF, nearline files larger than 45TB are not automatically backed up to tape.

retention.stated: Tenured infrastructure; data survives, but the allocation expires and the archival quota can be clawed back after project end - treat as renewable-while-funded, not permanent.
retention.notes: The FAQ reserves to the facilities the right to limit the amount and duration of archival storage after a project ends. At OLCF, retention is the period after project end or account deactivation: non-purged data is kept 90 days before the center may delete it, and work areas are purged after 90 days without access.

egress.terms: Globus/GridFTP and SSH transfer free to allocation holders; no egress meter. Data is not a public HTTP origin.

tooling: SSH/scp/sftp, Globus, Lustre + HPSS/Kronos nearline mounts; no S3.
chaining: One allocation = one project directory on a 100+ PB Lustre (Eagle/Orion) plus up to 200 TB nearline archive. Storage is not separately metered, so a storage-heavy proposal can request a large quota against a small compute request - but the proposal must still justify compute.
limits_note: Annual call only (mid-April to mid/late June), awards 1-3 years with a peer-reviewed annual renewal request. Post-project archival storage is explicitly at the facility's discretion ('The facilities reserve the right to limit the amount and duration of archival storage once a project has been completed'). Data must be research data; personal/non-work use prohibited.
